data.body:
Premise CONFIRMED in current tree. Every failed LLM call funnels through one seam (PydanticAIRunner.run except block, runner.py:573) which writes a JSONL spend row but nothing in-memory; ~13 swallow sites across src/rebar/llm/ each log a warning and return a default. The plan-review verdict has no counter for survived failures: coverage.resolution_class fires only on a FATAL degrade, and coverage.chunk_errors (pass1.py) is write-only with no reader and covers Pass-1 chunks only. So an overlap[] emptied by three dead judge batches is byte-identical to one emptied by "nothing overlapped".

Plan review: BLOCK on first pass (AC5 named the text renderer without citing it), PASS on second. Note the reviewer mis-cited the renderer as _render_review_text:677 (that is _scan_spec); review-plan actually renders via _render_plan_review_text:587. AC5 now cites the correct one.

Implemented as observability only: new stdlib-only leaf module src/rebar/llm/step_failures.py (contextvar sink mirroring review_kernel/telemetry.py, lock-guarded increments), recorded at the runner seam, activated in the plan-review run scope in gate_dispatch, drained into coverage.llm_step_failures in workflow_ops using the verification_contract_violations posture (present ONLY when non-empty, so a clean run stays byte-identical and attestation-safe). Leaf module was required, not preferred: runner.py (790) and structured_run.py (796) were both already at the 800-LOC cap.

11 held-out tests pass, incl. a wiring test that drives the REAL runner to failure offline and asserts the tally reaches the drain. make lint + make typecheck green. Lint initially failed the shrink-only complexity ratchet (_render_plan_review_text 16->18); fixed by extracting _render_step_failures rather than raising the frozen baseline.
